subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Which bounded core recovery contract should OpenClaw own for terminal provider model-unavailable errors that surface during subagent completion announce delivery?
rationale: The source shows several plausible fix layers, and choosing among provider classification, announce delivery semantics, config hot-reload validation, and watchdog recovery changes user-visible runtime behavior.

options.title: Approve bounded runtime fix
options.body: Classify terminal model-unavailable errors, prevent announce cleanup from amplifying requester history polling, and guarantee a blocked or failed parent completion without bundling config validation or watchdog scope.

options.title: Split the scope first
options.body: Keep this issue as the runtime announce/provider bug and move config reload validation or systemd watchdog recovery into the linked follow-up issues before implementation.

options.title: Wait for a canonical PR
options.body: Keep this issue open until one merged PR proves both the provider-error and announce-storm paths are covered, then close with implementation proof.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded runtime fix
recommendation.body: Classify terminal model-unavailable errors, prevent announce cleanup from amplifying requester history polling, and guarantee a blocked or failed parent completion without bundling config validation or watchdog scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work is closest to the subagent completion announce delivery boundary where the core recovery contract must be chosen.
